decisions.issues: v08 (the only candidate) fails on setting and balloon tails. (1) Setting: it shows a stone dungeon with masonry blocks, an iron wall ring and a sunlit barred window. That reads as the Goa cells, not the wooden ship's hold of panels 5.1 and 5.4 (timber planks, pen uprights, prisoner shelves, lantern and grating light). The warm window light also breaks the lighting continuity. (2) Balloons: the count is right (three), but the tails are wrong. The middle balloon (line 2, Keshavrao) points down at Nagoji's head. The right balloon (line 3, Nagoji) points at Keshavrao's head. Both tails end at hair rather than a mouth. Everything else works: both likenesses match their sheets (Nagoji has a clean-shaven chin, curled moustache and gold stud; Keshavrao has short ragged hair, a faint moustache, a grey-brown tunic and no stud), Keshavrao's tired half-smile and Nagoji's steady look hit the beat, the collars and manacles are right, and the hands are sound.
decisions.correction: SETTING FIX: this is NOT a stone dungeon. Set the two-shot inside the same wooden ship's hold as the neighbouring panels 5.1 and 5.4. Behind them: dark tarred timber hull planks and curved ribs, the plank upright of their pen, and an iron ring bolted to the beam off to one side, with one slack chain drooping from their collars to it. Behind that, shelves of other chained prisoners in grey, brown and off-white rags fade into shadow. Light is dim warm lantern light with a faint cool grey shaft from a hatch grating above. No stone blocks, no masonry, no barred window, no daylight window. Keep exactly what worked: Nagoji on the left (clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache, small gold ear stud, long loose curly hair, torn ochre sleeveless tunic, bandaged wrists, iron collar, chained manacles), looking steadily at Keshavrao. Keshavrao on the right (short ragged hair, faint moustache, grey-brown tunic, no ear stud), wearing his tired first half-smile. Both are seated with manacled hands resting on their knees. BALLOONS: exactly three blank white speech balloons in reading order, each tail ending at the speaker's mouth. Balloon 1 sits top left above Nagoji, with its tail running down to Nagoji's mouth. Balloon 2 sits top right above Keshavrao, a little lower than balloon 1, with its tail running down to Keshavrao's mouth. Balloon 3 sits lower, at the left edge beside Nagoji's head at mouth height, clear of his face and hair, with a short tail to Nagoji's mouth. No tail may cross the other character's head or stop at hair.

decisions.issues: Acceptable with minor deviations. (1) The sailors are front-lit and fully detailed rather than silhouetted. The officer is only half silhouetted: his face is shadowed in profile, but his gold buttons, cravat, red sash and lace cuffs show. (2) The 4th balloon's tail (final OFFICER line) aims at the officer's cravat and chest, about a head below his mouth. It still clearly indicates him. Balloon 1 points to the laughing sailor on the coaming and balloon 2 to the officer's face. The caption box is tailless, and the order is right: four blank areas, all in the sky, clear of faces. (3) Nagoji's ear stud is tiny and reads pale rather than gold. His chin has captivity stubble, which the bible allows. (4) The dhoti has saturated rust-brown blotches that could be mistaken for dried blood at a glance, though they match the stained captivity dhoti in neighbouring panels. The script beat is otherwise delivered: an up-angle through the open hatch at a bright sky, one sailor leaning on the coaming laughing, an officer in a tricorne, light pouring onto upturned, sick faces, and Nagoji lit and narrow-eyed at the lower edge in collar, bandaged wrists and chained manacles. There is no painted text, the hands are sound and nothing is anachronistic.

v07 (the only candidate) gets the faces right: Nagoji has the curled moustache, a clean chin with light stubble and the gold stud, and Keshavrao has short hair, a faint moustache and the grey-brown tunic. The setting also works: a slatted hull pen, a dipper on a peg, a trough and a wet floor with no rain. But the balloons are in the wrong reading order. The first balloon (top-left, highest, tail to Nagoji) would carry Nagoji's answer before Keshavrao's question, which the script gives first. The second balloon (right, tail to Keshavrao) comes later. Both tails also miss the mouths: Nagoji's ends at his ear stud and Keshavrao's ends on the crown of his hair. Costume misses: Nagoji's visible bare ankle and foot (bottom left) has no iron cuff or hobble chain, and his two wrist cuffs are not joined by their own short chain. The script beat is also weak: the frame barely reads as canted (the dipper and its drips hang dead vertical, the trough water is level), and the pen is fairly brightly lit rather than near dark.
decisions.correction: Keep v07's composition: Nagoji seated on the left in the torn ochre tunic with bandaged wrists, and Keshavrao on the right, knees drawn up and shivering, braced against the upright plank. Keep the slatted hull behind them, the dipper on its peg at right, the water trough at lower right, the wet planks, and the one slack chain from a ring on the beam running low between their two iron collars. Fix the balloon order. Keshavrao speaks FIRST, so his blank balloon must be the highest: put it touching the top border across the upper centre-right, with its tail running in front of everything and ending at Keshavrao's open mouth. Put Nagoji's blank balloon clearly lower: its top edge must sit below the bottom edge of Keshavrao's balloon, at the left edge beside Nagoji's head. Move the ring there onto the beam off to the right if needed. Its short tail must end at Nagoji's mouth, not his ear, and neither balloon may cover a face or hand. Tilt the whole frame a few degrees so the dipper hangs visibly off true from the plank and the trough water has slopped against one side. Darken the pen to near dark with the hatch shut, lit only by thin grey light through the plank seams. Show an iron cuff on every visible ankle of both men, joined by a short hobble chain. Join Nagoji's two wrist manacles by their own short chain about a forearm long.

decisions.issues: v07 (the only candidate) gets most of the storm beat. The frame is clearly canted about ten degrees. A heavy spare chain swings well off true from an overhead beam ring, attached to no one. A grey hatch seam overhead is broken by the shadows of running feet, with no sky, lightning or rain. A prisoner at the far right prays with his eyes shut. Water sloshes across the planks, and a single outlined blank caption box sits top-left with no tail, clear of faces. Nagoji (left) matches his sheet: curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud, bandaged forearms, collar and chained manacles. But Keshavrao has no iron collar (his throat is bare above the tunic) and no manacle on either wrist, which breaks the chained captivity shown in 6.1 to 6.4 and the script's 'both pairs of wrists'. His hand also rests on Nagoji's bandaged forearm near the elbow, not over Nagoji's bandaged hand. The trough slid against the upright is missing.
decisions.correction: Keep v07's composition and storm staging: the whole frame canted about ten degrees, the unattached spare chain swinging off true from the overhead beam ring, and the grey hatch seam with running-feet shadows (no sky, no rain falling indoors). Keep the eyes-shut praying prisoner at the far right, the water sloshing across the planks, and the single blank outlined caption box at top-left with no tail. Keep Nagoji on the left exactly as drawn. Keshavrao, on the right, must wear the same hinged iron collar as in 6.1. The one slack chain runs low between his collar and Nagoji's collar to a ring on the beam behind them, never taut or vertical above a head. Put iron manacles on both of Keshavrao's wrists, joined by a short chain. Put the joined hands in plain view in the lower middle of the frame. Keshavrao's thin, unbandaged fingers must lie over the back of Nagoji's bandaged HAND, not his forearm or elbow, with both men's wrist manacles and chains visible around the clasp. Add the wooden trough slid hard against the upright post of the pen.
